brief.analysis: Chips have run far ahead of the broader Nasdaq, and on the numbers the stretch is real and confirmed by the trend-adjusted read. But the reason is structural, not a fluke: hyperscaler AI spending is projected to run toward $1.2 trillion, giving semiconductors a durably larger share of the tech index than five years ago. Getting back to the old 5-year average would require a ~70% collapse in the relationship — that mean has almost certainly moved, so the statistics here are a trap, not a signal.
brief.report_line: We would not short semiconductors against the Nasdaq: the ~70% gap to the old average reflects a genuine AI-capex shift in index share, not a dislocation likely to reverse.

brief.analysis: The strongest case for a permanently higher gold-to-stocks relationship is that central banks are buying gold at record, structurally elevated levels, which pushed gold to all-time highs in 2025 and could keep it richer against stocks than history suggests. That said, this trade only needs a modest snap-back, and the ratio has already reverted: it hit its 200-day-average target and now sits close to normal, with the trend-adjusted read agreeing there's little stretch left. The near target is valid and largely captured; the deeper 5-year-average target (another ~13% lower) is the part where the old mean may no longer hold.
brief.report_line: Short gold versus stocks: the easy snap-back to the 200-day average is done, so we'd size this modestly and not chase the deeper target, because record central-bank gold buying may have permanently lifted where gold trades against equities.

brief.analysis: The strongest case for a lasting change is that silver's rally rests on record industrial demand, flat mine supply and falling inventories, with several forecasters seeing further upside — so silver may stay richer against gold than its history implies. Against that, the ratio has already reverted hard from an extreme peak, hit its 200-day-average target, and now trades only modestly above normal. The near target looks valid, but the deeper 5-year-average target (another ~18% lower) leans on a silver-versus-gold relationship that industrial demand may have structurally raised.
brief.report_line: Short silver versus gold back toward its recent trend only: the sharp move is largely retraced, so we'd take profits near the 200-day average rather than press toward the old mean given silver's structural industrial-demand tailwind.

brief.analysis: Metals and miners have run well ahead of the broad market, and the strongest structural argument is that copper and the same AI-capex build-out are lifting the sector on a multi-year view, which can keep miners richer against stocks than the past five years suggest. But the ratio has already snapped back to its 200-day-average target and sits only slightly stretched now, and the historical sample behind this signal is thin (just two prior episodes). The near reversion looks real; the deeper 5-year-average target (~22% lower) assumes a mean that the metals cycle may have shifted upward.
brief.report_line: Short metals-and-miners versus the market only back to trend, in small size: the snap-back to the 200-day average is largely done and a copper/AI-capex upcycle argues against pressing toward the old, possibly stale, average.
